subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw keep compaction and memoryFlush serialized with foreground session turns and rely on shorter timeouts/watchdog recovery, or introduce a dedicated/preemptible maintenance lane for that work?
rationale: The source-level problem is credible, but the durable fix changes scheduler fairness, transcript ordering, active-run ownership, and session recovery semantics across agent and channel paths.

options.title: Add a bounded maintenance lane
options.body: Create a dedicated or preemptible compaction/memoryFlush path with explicit ordering and recovery rules so foreground messages do not wait behind long maintenance work.

options.title: Keep current lanes with stronger recovery
options.body: Preserve strict serialization and improve watchdog cancellation, user notices, and recovery for long compaction instead of changing lane ownership.

options.title: Split into narrower trackers
options.body: Keep this issue as a canonical umbrella only until separate lane isolation, timeout recovery, and visibility issues fully own the remaining behavior.

recommendation.title: Add a bounded maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Create a dedicated or preemptible compaction/memoryFlush path with explicit ordering and recovery rules so foreground messages do not wait behind long maintenance work.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and GitHub commit metadata tie the active compaction/session-lane implementation paths to steipete, making this the clearest owner signal available from this checkout.
